polyoxide-relay 0.37.1: BENIGN, Polymarket relay API client.
Predecessor: https://static.crates.io/crates/polyoxide-relay/polyoxide-relay-0.37.0.crate
Full unpacked diff: source, examples, tests and README unchanged; version, VCS
revision and polyoxide-core version/checksum changed. Fetched and diffed core
0.37.0/0.37.1 too: only gzip configuration changed from bool to Option<bool>,
restoring reqwest's default unless explicitly overridden, with matching tests.
Flagged keys construct local Alloy signers; transaction signatures and addresses
are sent to the relay, not raw private keys. No new hook, payload or export.

ioredis 4.9.5: BENIGN, Node.js Redis client.
Predecessor: https://registry.npmjs.org/ioredis/-/ioredis-4.9.4.tgz
Full unpacked diff: README unchanged, including NAT example 203.0.113.73;
version/changelog and built/cluster/index.js changed. Cluster refresh now chains
setTimeout callbacks rather than overlapping setInterval and queries CLUSTER
SLOTS on a duplicate connection, disconnecting afterward. This avoids blocking
commands such as BLPOP blocking topology refresh. Dependencies/scripts unchanged.
NAT mapping is caller-configured and socket targets are Redis endpoints.
Both alerts' evidence predates these releases: detection drift, not compromise.

Placement review: secret-name environment reads belong in os/env/secret-name,
not credential theft; IPv4 host properties belong in communications/ip/endpoint,
not proxy identification or traffic collection. Nearest leaves env/read and
ip/literal lose to the explicit secret name and endpoint host property.
Neither matcher establishes an attacker objective. Moves retain effective
file/platform scopes. Exact curl-wallet-transfer, browser relay and Telegram
consumers updated; broad objective directory selectors intentionally stop
counting these neutral observations as attack evidence. No legacy aliases.
Separate matcher fixes: Rust call nodes exclude comments/string examples;
host-table query rejects RFC 5737 ranges and invalid octets/leading zeros.
Resolver/private exclusions retained. Count is AST captures, not distinct hosts;
renamed description says multiple rather than five proxies.

Validation evidence: atomscan and cleave facts on both samples; source/call
inspection; complete predecessor diffs and Rust dependency diff; positive and
near-miss fixtures for signing reads, comments, IP host tables, resolvers,
documentation ranges and malformed addresses. Synthetic curl wallet export
still fires hostile; browser relay consumer still fires. Archive scans have
zero suspicious and zero hostile findings. No package-name allowlisting.
